name: Kidney stones
overview: Kidney stones are hard deposits that form in the kidneys from waste products in the blood. Small stones often pass out in urine on their own, but larger ones can cause severe pain and may need treatment.
symptoms: Severe pain in the side of the tummy or back that may spread to the groin
Feeling restless and unable to get comfortable
Needing to pee more often or pain when peeing
causes: Waste chemicals such as calcium or uric acid building up and forming crystals
Not drinking enough fluids, making urine concentrated
riskFactors: A diet high in salt or animal protein
Family history or previous kidney stones
diagnosis: Kidney stones are diagnosed with urine and blood tests and a scan, usually a CT scan.
treatment: Procedures to break up or remove larger stones, such as shockwave treatment or ureteroscopy
selfCare: Drink plenty of water throughout the day so urine is pale
Strain your urine if advised, to collect the stone for testing
prevention: Follow specific diet advice for your stone type
whenToSeeDoctor: Pain in the side or back that comes and goes
Blood in urine
Recurring urine infections
emergencySigns: Severe pain with high temperature and shivering
Pain so severe you cannot get comfortable or stop vomiting
Unable to pee

name: Chronic kidney disease (CKD)
overview: Chronic kidney disease is a long-term condition where the kidneys do not work as well as they should. It is common, especially in older people, and often causes no symptoms in the early stages. Treatment can slow it down and lower the risk of heart disease.
symptoms: Usually no symptoms in early stages
Blood in urine or needing to pee more at night
causes: Kidney infections, inflammation or inherited kidney conditions
Long-term use of some medicines such as anti-inflammatory painkillers
riskFactors: Being of South Asian, African or African-Caribbean descent
diagnosis: CKD is diagnosed with blood tests (to estimate kidney function) and urine tests, often found during routine checks for people at risk.
treatment: Controlling blood pressure and blood sugar
Medicines to protect the kidneys and heart
Dialysis or kidney transplant for kidney failure
selfCare: Check with a doctor or pharmacist before taking new medicines
whenToSeeDoctor: You have diabetes or high blood pressure and have not had kidney checks
Persistent symptoms such as swollen ankles or tiredness
Blood in urine
emergencySigns: Severe shortness of breath
Passing very little or no urine
Chest pain or confusion

name: Urinary incontinence
overview: Urinary incontinence means accidentally passing urine. It is common, especially in women and older people, and is often treatable. Many people feel embarrassed, but doctors can help.
symptoms: Leaking urine when coughing, sneezing, laughing or exercising (stress incontinence)
A sudden, intense urge to pee, with leaking before reaching the toilet (urge incontinence)
Needing to pee often, including at night
causes: Weakened pelvic floor muscles, often after pregnancy and childbirth
diagnosis: A GP asks about symptoms, may examine you, and may test your urine or ask you to keep a bladder diary.
treatment: Surgery or procedures in some cases
selfCare: Cut down on caffeine and alcohol
whenToSeeDoctor: Any leaking of urine that affects your life
Incontinence starting suddenly
Blood in urine or pain when peeing
emergencySigns: Sudden loss of bladder control with numbness around the bottom or weakness in the legs
Unable to pee at all with tummy pain

name: Benign prostate enlargement (BPH)
overview: Benign prostate enlargement is when the prostate gland gets bigger, which is common in men over 50. It is not cancer and does not raise the risk of prostate cancer, but it can affect how you pee.
symptoms: Needing to pee more often or urgently
Feeling that the bladder has not fully emptied
causes: The exact cause is not fully understood
diagnosis: A GP asks about symptoms and may do a urine test, a blood test (PSA) and a rectal examination to check the prostate.
treatment: Medicines to relax the prostate or shrink it
selfCare: Cut down on caffeine and alcohol
Empty your bladder twice in a row (double voiding)
prevention: There is no proven way to prevent it; a healthy lifestyle may help
whenToSeeDoctor: Any changes in how you pee
Symptoms affecting sleep or daily life
Blood in urine
emergencySigns: Unable to pee at all, with a painful, swollen tummy
Pee problems with high temperature and shivering

name: Endometriosis
overview: Endometriosis is a long-term condition where tissue similar to the lining of the womb grows in other places, such as the ovaries and fallopian tubes. It can cause painful periods and pelvic pain, and can affect fertility. Treatments can help manage symptoms.
symptoms: Period pain that stops you doing normal activities
Pain in the lower tummy or back (pelvic pain)
Pain when pooing or peeing during a period
causes: Possible factors include genetics, immune system problems and menstrual blood flowing backwards into the pelvis
riskFactors: Starting periods at a young age
diagnosis: Endometriosis can be suspected from symptoms and scans, but is often confirmed by keyhole surgery (laparoscopy).
treatment: Hormone treatments such as the contraceptive pill or other hormonal medicines
selfCare: Use heat pads or warm baths for pain
prevention: There is no known way to prevent endometriosis
whenToSeeDoctor: Period pain that affects daily life
Pain during sex
Difficulty getting pregnant
Symptoms not improving with treatment
emergencySigns: Sudden, severe pelvic pain with fainting or feeling very unwell

name: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
overview: PCOS is a common condition that affects how the ovaries work. It can cause irregular periods, excess hair growth and difficulty getting pregnant. Symptoms can be managed, and it is linked to a higher risk of type 2 diabetes.
symptoms: Excess hair growth on the face, chest, back or buttocks
Thinning hair or hair loss from the head
causes: Linked to higher levels of hormones such as testosterone, and insulin resistance
diagnosis: PCOS is diagnosed from symptoms, blood tests for hormones, and sometimes an ultrasound scan of the ovaries.
treatment: Lifestyle changes such as weight loss if overweight
Medicines for excess hair or acne
Fertility treatments if trying to get pregnant
prevention: Healthy weight and regular activity can reduce symptoms and long-term risks
whenToSeeDoctor: Irregular or missed periods
Difficulty getting pregnant
Excess hair growth or hair loss

name: Menopause
overview: Menopause is when periods stop due to lower hormone levels, usually between ages 45 and 55. Perimenopause is the time before, when symptoms often start. Symptoms can be managed with lifestyle changes and treatments such as hormone replacement therapy.
symptoms: Changes to periods, becoming irregular before stopping
Low mood, anxiety or mood swings
Vaginal dryness and reduced sex drive
causes: Natural fall in oestrogen and other hormones with age
riskFactors: Early menopause can run in families
diagnosis: Menopause is usually diagnosed from symptoms in people over 45; blood tests may be used in younger people.
treatment: Vaginal oestrogen or lubricants for dryness
Talking therapies such as CBT for mood and sleep
selfCare: Healthy diet with enough calcium and vitamin D
Wear light layers and keep the bedroom cool
Limit caffeine, alcohol and spicy food if they trigger flushes
prevention: Menopause is natural and cannot be prevented, but bone and heart health can be protected with exercise and a healthy diet
whenToSeeDoctor: Symptoms affecting your daily life
Symptoms of menopause before age 45
Bleeding after periods have stopped for 12 months

name: Erectile dysfunction
overview: Erectile dysfunction is when you cannot get or keep an erection. It is very common, especially with age, and can be a sign of other health problems such as heart disease or diabetes. Effective treatments are available.
symptoms: Difficulty keeping an erection during sex
Reduced sexual desire in some cases
causes: Physical causes such as narrowed blood vessels, high blood pressure, diabetes or hormone problems
Psychological causes such as stress, anxiety or depression
riskFactors: Heart disease, diabetes or high blood pressure
diagnosis: A GP or sexual health clinic asks about symptoms and may check blood pressure, blood sugar, cholesterol and hormone levels.
treatment: Medicines that increase blood flow to the penis, prescribed by a doctor or pharmacist
prevention: Control blood pressure, cholesterol and diabetes
whenToSeeDoctor: Erection problems that keep happening
You have other symptoms such as chest pain or breathlessness on exertion
emergencySigns: An erection lasting more than 4 hours (priapism)
Chest pain during sexual activity

name: Vaginal thrush
overview: Vaginal thrush is a common yeast infection. It is not usually serious, is not a sexually transmitted infection, and can be treated with pharmacy medicines.
symptoms: White vaginal discharge, often like cottage cheese, which does not usually smell
Itching and irritation around the vagina
Soreness and stinging during sex or when peeing
causes: Overgrowth of Candida yeast, which normally lives harmlessly in the body
Changes that upset the natural balance in the vagina, such as antibiotics, hormone changes or high blood sugar
diagnosis: Thrush is often recognised from symptoms; a GP or sexual health clinic may take a swab if it keeps coming back or the diagnosis is unclear.
treatment: Antifungal pessaries, creams or tablets from a pharmacy or prescribed by a doctor
selfCare: Use water and emollient instead of soap to wash
prevention: Control blood sugar if you have diabetes
whenToSeeDoctor: It is your first time having symptoms
You are pregnant or under 16
Treatment has not worked or thrush keeps coming back
Unusual discharge, smell, bleeding or sores

name: Glaucoma
overview: Glaucoma is a group of eye conditions where the optic nerve is damaged, usually by fluid building up in the eye. It often develops slowly without symptoms, so regular eye tests are important. Early treatment can prevent sight loss.
symptoms: In acute glaucoma: sudden intense eye pain, red eye and headache
causes: Build-up of fluid in the eye that increases pressure and damages the optic nerve
Sometimes damage occurs with normal eye pressure
riskFactors: Being of African, Caribbean or Asian descent
diagnosis: Glaucoma is detected during eye tests by measuring eye pressure, examining the optic nerve, and testing the field of vision.
treatment: Eye drops to lower eye pressure
selfCare: Use eye drops exactly as prescribed
Tell the driving authority if required in your country
prevention: Regular eye tests, especially if over 40 or with a family history
whenToSeeDoctor: You have a family history of glaucoma and have not had an eye test recently
Gradual changes in vision
emergencySigns: Sudden intense eye pain with a red eye
Sudden blurred vision or seeing halos around lights with headache, nausea or vomiting

name: Cataracts
overview: Cataracts are when the lens inside the eye becomes cloudy, causing blurred or misty vision. They are very common in older people. Surgery to replace the cloudy lens is safe and effective.
symptoms: Finding lights too bright or glaring
causes: Natural changes in the lens with age
Diabetes, eye injury, long-term steroid use, or sun exposure
diagnosis: Cataracts are diagnosed during an eye test by an optometrist or eye specialist.
treatment: Stronger glasses and brighter lighting in early stages
Surgery to replace the cloudy lens with an artificial one
whenToSeeDoctor: Vision is becoming blurry or cloudy
Vision problems affecting daily life such as reading or driving
emergencySigns: Sudden loss of vision
Severe eye pain or redness after cataract surgery

name: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD)
overview: Age-related macular degeneration affects the middle part of your vision. It usually affects people over 50 and does not cause total blindness, but it can make everyday activities like reading and recognising faces difficult. Wet AMD can be treated if found early.
causes: Damage to the macula, part of the retina, with ageing
Dry AMD develops slowly; wet AMD is caused by abnormal blood vessels and can develop quickly
diagnosis: AMD is diagnosed during an eye examination, usually with a scan of the back of the eye (OCT).
treatment: Injections into the eye for wet AMD
No treatment yet to reverse dry AMD; support and low-vision aids help
selfCare: Eat a healthy diet with leafy greens
whenToSeeDoctor: Gradual changes in central vision
Difficulty reading or seeing fine detail
emergencySigns: Sudden distortion of vision or straight lines appearing wavy (get seen urgently by an eye specialist)
Sudden loss of vision

name: Tinnitus
overview: Tinnitus is hearing noises such as ringing or buzzing that are not caused by an outside source. It is common and often linked to hearing loss. It may improve over time, and there are ways to manage it.
symptoms: Ringing, buzzing, humming, whooshing or hissing sounds
Sounds that come and go or are constant
causes: Hearing loss from ageing or loud noise
diagnosis: A GP looks in the ears and may refer you for hearing tests with an audiologist or ear specialist.
treatment: Treating the cause, such as removing earwax
Hearing aids if hearing loss is present
selfCare: Use relaxing background sounds, especially at night
Protect your ears from loud noise
prevention: Use ear protection around loud noise
whenToSeeDoctor: Tinnitus that does not go away or is getting worse
Tinnitus affecting sleep, concentration or mood
Tinnitus in one ear only
Tinnitus that beats in time with your pulse
emergencySigns: Tinnitus after a head injury
Sudden hearing loss, dizziness or weakness in the face

name: Hearing loss
overview: Hearing loss is very common, especially as people get older. It can happen gradually or suddenly. Sometimes it is temporary and treatable, such as from earwax, and hearing aids help many people with long-term hearing loss.
symptoms: Difficulty hearing other people clearly or misunderstanding them
Turning the TV up louder than others want
Difficulty hearing on the phone or in noisy places
causes: Some medicines or conditions such as Ménière's disease
riskFactors: Loud noise exposure at work or leisure
diagnosis: A GP looks in the ears and refers for hearing tests by an audiologist if needed.
treatment: Cochlear implants for severe hearing loss
selfCare: Do not use cotton buds in the ears
Ask people to face you when speaking
prevention: Have hearing checked if you notice changes
whenToSeeDoctor: Hearing is gradually getting worse
Hearing loss in one ear
Hearing loss with ear pain or discharge
emergencySigns: Sudden hearing loss in one or both ears (seek urgent help the same day)
Hearing loss after a head injury
Hearing loss with sudden dizziness, weakness or facial drooping
